exposure: Colour Doppler Ultrasonography (USG) findings (umbilical artery's resistance index (RI), pulsatility index (PI), and peak systolic velocity (PSV))
cohort: Pregnant participants who underwent Colour Doppler USG between 24 and 36 weeks of gestation.
finding: Abnormal umbilical artery Doppler indices were significantly associated with lower birth weight, higher rates of caesarean delivery, and increased NICU admissions, identifying Colour Doppler USG as an effective tool for predicting adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Abnormal Doppler indices were associated with higher rates of caesarean delivery (62.5% vs. 28.1%, p < 0.001).
followup_time: At birth or immediate neonatal period
